prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Production illustrated Kazi sword animation, preserving the approved character style and body proportions.
Image 1 is the original recovered attack, for facing, body action and violet slash/explosion visual language. Image 2 is the APPROVED NEUTRAL CHARACTER of this SAME view and the authoritative head/torso proportions. Image 3 is the identity and LONG SLIM CURVED SWORD reference. Face north west (back-left); keep the same weapon hand, clothes, head/skull/hair shape, marked face, white collar, gold waist buttons, trousers and boots. For rear views show his back.
Create EXACTLY 11 sequential frames in a 4-column by 3-row uniform grid; last cell empty. This corrects the old illustrated sheet where the character held almost the same sword pose while effects changed. The hand, blade, arms, shoulders and hips MUST really move through the following sequence, with one thin curved sword continuously gripped in his original hand:
Frame 0: READY, upright neutral combat stance as image 2, sword quiet, NO big slash effect.
Frame 1: HIP POSITION, pull the sword hand clearly back to his hip/waist, elbow bent, blade near the hip, shoulders start to coil. NO crescent/explosion.
Frame 2: WIDE WIND-UP, hips and shoulders rotate into a readable large backswing at the hip; blade still drawn back, torso and legs prepare the cut. Only tiny purple sparks.
Frame 3: begin the fast RIGHTWARD hip-level draw-cut; body uncoils and the hand carries the sword from the hip toward the right in the east-facing preview. A short violet trail follows the actual blade.
Frame 4: MIDDLE of the broad rightward slash, arm and sword sweeping across/forward, hips turn, a wide purple crescent follows that exact path.
Frame 5: finish the rightward slash, extended follow-through, crescent opens away from him. This is the first cut's contact pose.
Frame 6: recover the same sword upward, elbow bends and the sword hand rises above shoulder/head level to prepare a DOWNWARD cut; trail only, NO explosion yet.
Frame 7: actual DOWNWARD SLASH, blade and hand travel from high to low in front of him, torso follows and knees bend. A narrow diagonal/vertical violet streak follows the blade down.
Frame 8: finish low, sword hand toward the ground in the follow-through; the first bright white-violet IMPACT EXPLOSION appears ahead of the blade at the end of that cut.
Frame 9: final purple-white explosion opens wide with the original sharp diagonal energy, while Kazi holds a low completed-cut pose.
Frame 10: explosion dissipates in shards/sparks, Kazi recovers from the low follow-through, sword still in his hand. Final cell 11 empty.
The rightward cut and downward cut must be TWO visibly distinct sword/body motions, rotated consistently for this facing. Preserve the original hand; do not mirror handedness. No fixed arm beneath an independently animated explosion, no second weapon, ghost swords, sword detached from hand, early explosion, thrust-only attack, or unchanged body repeated across the sheet.
Keep character anatomy and scale IDENTICAL throughout all 11 frames and to image 2. A pose may bend naturally, but the body/head must never inflate, shrink or stretch. Keep one shared hip/ground origin per cell and feet on the same baseline. The end explosion may be large like image 1 but may not resize Kazi.
Transparent production sprite sheet, same canvas aspect as image 1. Keep the full body, longer blade and EVERY effect at least 20 clear transparent pixels inside EACH cell; uniformly fit all artwork within the cell, never crop energy or cross into neighbors. True alpha-zero background, no gray haze, backdrop, ground shadow, floor, text, frame labels, grid lines or watermark. Retain sharp approved hand-painted detail.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Make Kazi's run COMPACT without changing his approved illustrated identity or longer slim curved sword.
Image 1 is the current RUN SHEET edit target. Image 2 is the approved neutral character in the same view and the HEAD/TORSO PROPORTION authority. Image 3 is the identity and long thin curved sword reference. Face north west (back-left) with the original weapon hand.
Exactly 18 frames, 6 equal columns x 3 equal rows, one seamless full left/right run cycle. Preserve the same stern marked face, skull/head height and hair silhouette from image 2, charcoal split coat, white collar, gold buttons, trousers, boots, purple sparks and thin long curved blade. Change the running poses so they no longer look horizontally stretched, huge, or like an exaggerated long lunge.
Use a more upright torso (about 5-8 degrees lean), natural compact arms close to the torso, normal limb lengths. Keep the head outline/size from the neutral view; do NOT widen or fan the hair into a long aerodynamic shape. Reduce trailing coat/hair extension by about half versus image 1. The coat follows the body rather than extending as a long horizontal banner. Shorter, tighter leg reach: forward heel and rear toe each extend no farther than about 15% of standing body height from the hips. Preserve the long sword itself; compact the hand position close to his hip instead of shortening the blade.
Frame 0 LEFT heel contact slightly in front; frame 1 planted foot passes under hip; frame 2 travels behind hip; frame 3 rear toe-off. Frames 4,5,6,7,8 tuck/recover the left knee/boot forward naturally, opposite arm counter-swing. Frame 9 RIGHT heel contact; 10 passes beneath hip; 11 behind; 12 rear toe-off. Frames 13,14,15,16,17 recover the right knee/boot into the next frame 0 contact. Each planted foot travels steadily backward while its sole stays at one common floor baseline. In front/back/diagonal views foreshorten this same compact cycle. Eighteen distinct poses, no long holds, no slide-in-place feet fixed under torso.
Keep body/hip and head heights very steady: tiny natural bob below 1.5% of body height, no hops or exaggerated knee bounces. Same character proportions and uniform scale in every frame/row/direction. Preserve the shorter profile width through compact posing, NEVER by squashing the image or scaling the head sideways.
Exactly the same 6x3 grid/canvas aspect as image 1, same sharp illustrated style. At least 20 clear transparent pixels inside every cell boundary around body, limbs, longer sword and ALL sparks. Fit all art uniformly within cells, no clipping or neighbor overlap. True transparent alpha zero background, no haze, floor, ground shadows, grid, numbers, labels, extra frames or watermark.
